question: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

In August 2026, the Commission presented a proposal for Baltic fishing quotas in 2027. It provides for cuts in the bycatch limits for cod of 88% and 51% and an increase in the limits for sprat of 44%. In light of the above: 1.

Why does the Commission consider it proportionate and reasonable to further mechanically tighten restrictions on the fishing sector, given that the bans in force since 2019 have not led to the recovery of cod stocks and that factors not linked to fishing are having a significant impact on the situation?

When proposing to increase the catch limit for sprat by 44%, how did the Commission take into account the requirement to apply an ecosystem-based approach and the key importance of this species in the diet of cod?

How has the Commission assessed the risk that setting bycatch limits on the basis of the bycatch reported in 2025, in the absence of a level set by ICES, will lead to the premature closure of mixed fisheries and drastically impact the coastal fleet?
